subject: ShopWell - Dedicated capacity performance validation follow-up (SLOs & next steps)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: ShopWell - Dedicated capacity performance validation follow-up (SLOs & next steps)

Hi Sam - thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we all have alignment.

Recap of ShopWell SLOs (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 generation < 150 ms for typical prompt+response (<= 256 tokens). p99 for longer tails OK up to 300 ms, but prefer keep < 300 ms.
- Throughput: steady-state throughput target ~120k tokens/min (burst to 200k tokens/min for short windows).
- Concurrency: support for 40-64 concurrent active sessions.
- Streaming: chunked/streaming responses with < 50 ms between chunks to keep UI responsive.
- Model profile: mixture of retrieval-augmented generation and short prompt completions. Typical output lengths 64-256 tokens.

What we'll validate on Dedicated:
1) GPU comparison (H100 vs A100 config) for your workload - latency/throughput tradeoffs.
2) Reserved throughput sizing for the requested steady-state and burst capacity.
3) Concurrency behavior and prioritized streaming performance (end-to-end latency with streaming).
4) Quantization/precision experiments (fp16 -> int8 / tensor cores) to balance cost vs latency.

Attachments included: dedicated_capacity_benchmark_v1.pdf (initial benchmark templates), redwood_dedicated_sizing_sheet.xlsx (sizing workbook).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- We can provision a short validation run on a dedicated H100 pool for two business days (perf + streaming tests). Proposed window: Tue 2026-07-21 - Wed 2026-07-22.
- Aditya will coordinate test harness and the exact test corpus (we'll use the draft prompt set you shared and add 1000 synthetic short prompts to simulate traffic).
- After the run we'll deliver: (a) per-GPU latency and throughput table, (b) recommendations for reserved throughput and concurrency, (c) cost estimate and draft SLA.

Please confirm the window works and whether you want us to include an A100 comparison in the same run (adds ~6-8 hours to provisioning + analysis).

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ShopWell - Dedicated capacity performance validation follow-up (SLOs & next steps)

Thanks Alex - adding a few technical clarifications and the test plan outline so Sam has visibility.

Technical clarifications / plan notes:
- Model warm-start: for streaming p95 targets we'll need to consider cold vs warm KV-cache. Plan to run both warm (cached KV) and cold (first request) passes and report both numbers.
- Batch sizing: we'll test continuous batching settings: low-latency mode (batch size ~1-4, prioritized) and throughput mode (batching up to 32) to show tradeoffs.
- GPU kernels: H100 with latest cuDNN/Kernel updates will likely have better throughput at high concurrency, but A100 can be more cost-effective for steady-state. We'll provide per-token cost estimates.
- Network: we'll simulate your real-world token ingress using your sample distribution. Please confirm whether the test traffic should originate from us (Redwood controlled) or from your side to measure last-mile network differences.

Proposed test steps during the 2-day window:
1) Day 1 - baseline runs: 1) A100 (if opted) quick run; 2) H100 baseline runs - short prompts (64 tokens) and medium (256 tokens), streaming on/off.
2) Day 2 - concurrency/stress: increase concurrent sessions (10, 25, 40, 64) and simulate bursts to 200k tokens/min. Collect p50/p95/p99, QoE metrics for streaming (inter-chunk latency), and failure/retry rates.

I've attached the initial benchmark template (dedicated_capacity_benchmark_v1.pdf) - it has the exact metrics we'll produce.

If Sam confirms test origin and A100 inclusion, I'll kick off infra provisioning and share run credentials.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@shopwell.ai>

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ShopWell - Dedicated capacity performance validation follow-up (SLOs & next steps)

Alex / Aditya - thanks for the clear recap. The window (Jul 21-22) works for us. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming: critical. Our UI expects progressive tokens to appear within ~40-60ms; if chunked server-side we need inter-chunk latency < 50 ms overall.
2) Concurrency: target concurrency is 48 for launch (steady 40 with spikes to 64).
3) Throughput: confirm that "120k tokens/min steady" maps to your reserved throughput concept (we'd prefer a committed baseline with short bursts).
4) A100 vs H100: we'd like both comparisons. H100 preferred if it materially improves p95 at our concurrency; include per-hour cost delta.

Also please include a short column in the post-run report that maps observed latency to UX risk (green/yellow/red) so we can make rollout decisions.

Can you also include the draft SLA & pricing estimate prior to the run? I'll loop in procurement after we have the H100/A100 comparison and the draft SLA.

Thanks - Sam
Sam Carter
Head of AI Products
